unit.title: Đọc C1
unit.summary: Kinh tế học hành vi, thiên kiến xác nhận, kinh tế chú ý, hiệu ứng giả dược, thành phố 15 phút, thuật toán công bằng, ngôn ngữ và tư duy, ý niệm tiến bộ.

lessons.title: Cú hích hành vi
lessons.summary: Kinh tế học hành vi và thiết kế lựa chọn.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Classical economic theory rests on the assumption that people are rational: they weigh costs against benefits and choose whatever maximizes their well-being. Behavioral economics challenges this picture, drawing on psychology to show that human decisions are systematically shaped by habit, emotion and the way options are presented.
paragraphs.vi: Lý thuyết kinh tế cổ điển dựa trên giả định con người duy lý: họ cân nhắc chi phí và lợi ích rồi chọn điều tối đa hoá phúc lợi của mình. Kinh tế học hành vi thách thức bức tranh đó, dựa vào tâm lý học để cho thấy quyết định của con người bị chi phối một cách có hệ thống bởi thói quen, cảm xúc và cách các lựa chọn được trình bày.

paragraphs.en: One of the field's most influential ideas is the "nudge": a small change in the design of a choice that steers behavior without forbidding any option or significantly altering incentives. Placing fruit at eye level in a school cafeteria, for instance, tends to increase how much fruit students take, even though the chocolate remains available.
paragraphs.vi: Một trong những ý tưởng có ảnh hưởng nhất của lĩnh vực này là "cú hích": một thay đổi nhỏ trong thiết kế lựa chọn giúp định hướng hành vi mà không cấm phương án nào hay làm thay đổi đáng kể các động cơ khuyến khích. Chẳng hạn đặt trái cây ngang tầm mắt trong căng tin trường học thường làm học sinh lấy nhiều trái cây hơn, dù sô-cô-la vẫn có sẵn.

paragraphs.en: Default options are particularly powerful. When employees are automatically enrolled in a retirement savings plan and must actively opt out, participation rates are typically far higher than when they must actively sign up. The choice is identical in both cases; only the starting point differs.
paragraphs.vi: Lựa chọn mặc định đặc biệt mạnh. Khi nhân viên được tự động đăng ký vào chương trình tiết kiệm hưu trí và phải chủ động rút ra, tỷ lệ tham gia thường cao hơn nhiều so với khi họ phải chủ động đăng ký. Lựa chọn trong hai trường hợp là như nhau; chỉ điểm xuất phát khác nhau.

paragraphs.en: Critics, however, question whether governments and companies should be engineering choices at all. If nudges work precisely because people do not notice them, they may sit uneasily with the ideal of autonomous citizens. Defenders reply that there is no neutral design: every menu and every form presents options in some order, so the real question is not whether to influence choices, but how transparently and in whose interest.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên, người phê phán đặt câu hỏi liệu chính phủ và doanh nghiệp có nên thiết kế lựa chọn của người khác hay không. Nếu cú hích hiệu quả chính vì người ta không nhận ra nó, nó có thể khó dung hoà với lý tưởng về công dân tự chủ. Người bảo vệ đáp rằng không có thiết kế nào trung lập: thực đơn hay biểu mẫu nào cũng trình bày lựa chọn theo một thứ tự nào đó, nên câu hỏi thật sự không phải là có nên tác động đến lựa chọn hay không, mà là tác động minh bạch đến đâu và vì lợi ích của ai.

headings: Why the starting point of a choice matters
Healthier food choices in school cafeterias
A challenge to the idea of the rational decision-maker
A debate about the ethics of designing choices
Evidence that nudges save governments money
Guiding behavior without taking options away
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 contrasts classical rational choice with behavioral economics; paragraph 2 defines the nudge (the cafeteria is only an example); paragraph 3 is about default options; paragraph 4 sets critics against defenders. The passage never mentions saving government money.

exercises.prompt: Which of the following best defines a "nudge" as described in the text?
choices: A financial reward for making healthy choices
A rule that forbids harmful options
A subtle change to how a choice is arranged that leaves every option open
A campaign that explains the benefits of saving
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: a nudge is a small change in the design of a choice that does not forbid any option or significantly alter incentives, so it is neither a reward, a ban nor an information campaign.

exercises.prompt: What point does the retirement savings example illustrate?
choices: The starting point of a choice can strongly affect outcomes.
Employees dislike saving money.
Opting out should be made illegal.
Higher salaries increase participation.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: the choice is the same in both cases and only the starting point differs, yet participation is far higher — the default itself changes the outcome.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "steers" is closest in meaning to …
choices: forces
guides
slows
reveals
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: a nudge "steers behavior without forbidding any option", so it guides people in a direction rather than forcing them.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraph 3 about employees?
choices: They are legally required to stay in the retirement plan.
Many of them tend to keep whatever option has already been chosen for them.
Most of them compare plans carefully before deciding.
Retirement plans cost them less when enrollment is automatic.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: the choice is identical and opting out is possible, yet participation is far higher under automatic enrollment, so many people simply stay with the default. If they compared plans carefully, the starting point would not matter.

exercises.statement: In the cafeteria example, chocolate is removed to encourage students to eat fruit.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: the chocolate "remains available"; only the position of the fruit changes.

exercises.statement: Defenders of nudges claim that options can be presented without influencing people.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: defenders say "there is no neutral design" — every menu and form puts options in some order, so some influence is unavoidable.

exercises.statement: Nudges have been shown to work better in schools than in workplaces.
exercises.explain: The passage gives one school example and one workplace example but never compares how well nudges work in the two settings.

exercises.prompt: Classical economic theory assumes that people are ___.
choices: rational
emotional
generous
exercises.explain: Đoạn 1: "rests on the assumption that people are rational".

exercises.text: Behavioral economics rejects the classical view that choices result from a careful ___ of costs and benefits. A nudge changes the way options are ___, yet every alternative stays available. Defaults are a striking case: making enrollment automatic sharply increases ___. Critics worry that hidden nudges threaten personal ___, but defenders reply that no design is ever neutral.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: people are assumed to "weigh costs against benefits"; paragraph 2: a nudge changes the design of a choice "without forbidding any option"; paragraph 3: automatic enrollment gives "far higher" participation; paragraph 4: critics see a conflict with "autonomous citizens".

lessons.title: Thiên kiến xác nhận
lessons.summary: Vì sao ta chỉ thấy điều mình muốn tin.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

blocks.title: Seeing What We Expect to See

paragraphs.en: Of all the mental shortcuts that distort human judgment, confirmation bias is perhaps the most pervasive. It refers to the tendency to seek out, interpret and remember information in ways that support what we already believe, while giving less weight to evidence that contradicts it.
paragraphs.vi: Trong mọi lối tắt tư duy làm méo mó phán đoán của con người, thiên kiến xác nhận có lẽ phổ biến nhất. Nó chỉ xu hướng tìm kiếm, diễn giải và ghi nhớ thông tin theo cách ủng hộ điều ta vốn tin, trong khi xem nhẹ bằng chứng trái ngược.

paragraphs.en: The bias operates at several stages. When choosing what to read, we gravitate toward sources that share our views. When faced with ambiguous data, we interpret it charitably if it suits us and skeptically if it does not. Even memory is selective: experiments suggest that people recall the arguments that favored their position more accurately than those that opposed it.
paragraphs.vi: Thiên kiến này vận hành ở nhiều giai đoạn. Khi chọn đọc gì, ta bị hút về những nguồn cùng quan điểm. Khi gặp dữ liệu mơ hồ, ta diễn giải rộng lượng nếu nó hợp ý và hoài nghi nếu không. Ngay cả trí nhớ cũng có chọn lọc: thí nghiệm cho thấy người ta nhớ chính xác các lập luận ủng hộ mình hơn các lập luận phản đối.

paragraphs.en: Crucially, intelligence offers little protection. Some studies indicate that people with strong reasoning skills are simply better at constructing justifications for conclusions they reached for other reasons. Expertise can therefore make the bias harder, not easier, to detect.
paragraphs.vi: Điều then chốt là trí thông minh không bảo vệ được bao nhiêu. Một số nghiên cứu cho thấy người có kỹ năng lập luận tốt chỉ giỏi hơn trong việc dựng lý lẽ biện minh cho kết luận mà họ đã đi đến vì lý do khác. Vì thế chuyên môn có thể khiến thiên kiến khó phát hiện hơn chứ không dễ hơn.

paragraphs.en: Since the bias cannot be switched off, the most effective remedies are procedural rather than personal. Scientists pre-register their hypotheses before collecting data; well-run organizations appoint someone to argue deliberately against a proposed plan. At an individual level, one useful habit is to ask not "Is there evidence for my view?" but "What would convince me that I am wrong?"
paragraphs.vi: Vì không thể tắt thiên kiến, biện pháp hiệu quả nhất mang tính quy trình hơn là cá nhân. Nhà khoa học đăng ký trước giả thuyết trước khi thu thập dữ liệu; tổ chức vận hành tốt cử một người cố ý phản biện kế hoạch được đề xuất. Ở cấp cá nhân, một thói quen hữu ích là đừng hỏi "Có bằng chứng cho quan điểm của mình không?" mà hỏi "Điều gì sẽ thuyết phục mình rằng mình sai?"

headings: Why clever people are not safe from it
Training people to switch the bias off
What the bias is, and how widespread it is
Building safeguards into the way decisions are made
Bias at every stage of handling information
How scientists publish their results
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 defines the bias and calls it the most pervasive; paragraph 2 shows it at the stages of choosing, interpreting and remembering; paragraph 3 says intelligence and expertise give little protection; paragraph 4 describes procedural remedies. Paragraph 4 says the bias cannot be switched off, and publishing is never discussed.

exercises.prompt: According to the text, how does intelligence relate to confirmation bias?
choices: It largely eliminates the bias.
It has no connection to reasoning at all.
It makes people more open to opposing views.
It helps people justify conclusions reached for other reasons.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: people with strong reasoning skills are "better at constructing justifications for conclusions they reached for other reasons", so intelligence offers little protection.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred about a highly knowledgeable expert who holds a firm opinion?
choices: They are more willing than others to change their mind when shown contrary evidence.
They do not need procedures such as pre-registration.
Their expertise may make their bias harder to spot.
Their conclusions are always reached by careful reasoning alone.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: expertise "can make the bias harder, not easier, to detect", because skilled reasoners build better justifications. Paragraph 4 recommends procedures for everyone, and paragraph 3 says conclusions are often reached "for other reasons".

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 1, the word "pervasive" is closest in meaning to …
choices: harmful
widespread
obvious
recent
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: of all mental shortcuts, confirmation bias is "perhaps the most pervasive", meaning it is found everywhere; paragraph 2 then shows it at every stage of handling information.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer end with the question "What would convince me that I am wrong?"
choices: To show that individuals can switch the bias off completely
To offer a personal habit that works against looking only for support
To criticize scientists for not questioning their hypotheses
To argue that personal remedies work better than procedural ones
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: after the procedural remedies, the writer gives "one useful habit" at an individual level, which reverses the search for supporting evidence. The same paragraph says the bias "cannot be switched off" and that procedural remedies are the most effective.

exercises.statement: According to the text, people remember the arguments on their own side of a debate better than those against it.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: experiments suggest people "recall the arguments that favored their position more accurately than those that opposed it".

exercises.statement: The writer believes experts are immune to confirmation bias.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: intelligence offers little protection, and expertise can make the bias "harder, not easier, to detect".

exercises.statement: Confirmation bias is stronger in older people than in younger people.
exercises.explain: The passage never mentions age, so this cannot be checked against the text.

exercises.prompt: Scientists ___ their hypotheses before collecting data.
choices: pre-register
publish
abandon
exercises.explain: Đoạn 4: "Scientists pre-register their hypotheses before collecting data".

exercises.text: Confirmation bias makes people favor information that ___ what they already think. It affects what we choose to read, how we judge unclear ___, and even what we remember. A sharp mind gives little ___ against it, so the most reliable defenses are built into ___ rather than left to the individual.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: we look for information that supports existing beliefs; paragraph 2: ambiguous data is interpreted to suit us; paragraph 3: "intelligence offers little protection"; paragraph 4: the best remedies are "procedural rather than personal".

lessons.title: Kinh tế của sự chú ý
lessons.summary: Khi sự chú ý của bạn là món hàng.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: In an age of information abundance, the scarce resource is no longer information itself but the human attention required to process it. Many digital platforms are offered free of charge precisely because their real product is the attention of their users, which is sold to advertisers in the form of carefully targeted audiences.
paragraphs.vi: Trong thời đại thông tin dư thừa, nguồn lực khan hiếm không còn là bản thân thông tin mà là sự chú ý của con người cần để xử lý nó. Nhiều nền tảng số được cung cấp miễn phí chính vì sản phẩm thật của họ là sự chú ý của người dùng, được bán cho nhà quảng cáo dưới dạng nhóm khán giả nhắm mục tiêu kỹ lưỡng.

paragraphs.en: This business model creates powerful incentives. The longer users stay, the more advertisements they see, so platforms invest heavily in features that maximize engagement: endless feeds that never reach a natural stopping point, notifications timed to draw people back, and recommendation systems that learn which content is hardest to ignore.
paragraphs.vi: Mô hình kinh doanh này tạo ra động cơ mạnh. Người dùng ở lại càng lâu thì càng xem nhiều quảng cáo, nên nền tảng đầu tư mạnh vào tính năng tối đa hoá mức độ tương tác: bảng tin vô tận không bao giờ có điểm dừng tự nhiên, thông báo canh thời điểm để kéo người dùng quay lại, và hệ thống gợi ý học được nội dung nào khó bỏ qua nhất.

paragraphs.en: The difficulty is that content which captures attention is not necessarily content that serves users well. Material that provokes outrage or anxiety often spreads faster than calm, careful reporting. Over time, critics argue, an environment optimized for engagement may erode the capacity for sustained concentration on which learning and democratic debate depend.
paragraphs.vi: Vấn đề là nội dung thu hút sự chú ý không nhất thiết là nội dung phục vụ tốt người dùng. Nội dung gây phẫn nộ hay lo âu thường lan nhanh hơn tin tức điềm tĩnh, cẩn trọng. Về lâu dài, người phê phán cho rằng một môi trường được tối ưu cho tương tác có thể bào mòn khả năng tập trung bền bỉ mà việc học và tranh luận dân chủ phụ thuộc vào.

paragraphs.en: Proposed responses range from design regulations, such as banning certain manipulative features for minors, to alternative business models based on subscriptions. Individual strategies, like disabling notifications, help, but they place the burden on users to resist systems engineered by teams of specialists to be irresistible.
paragraphs.vi: Các giải pháp được đề xuất trải từ quy định về thiết kế, như cấm một số tính năng thao túng với trẻ vị thành niên, đến mô hình kinh doanh thay thế dựa trên thuê bao. Chiến lược cá nhân như tắt thông báo có ích, nhưng chúng đặt gánh nặng lên người dùng phải cưỡng lại những hệ thống được đội ngũ chuyên gia thiết kế để khó cưỡng lại.

headings: A gap between what holds attention and what is good for us
Evidence that people now read less news
Why users' attention is what is really being sold
Rules, new business models and the limits of self-help
How advertisers choose their target audiences
Features designed to keep people scrolling
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 explains that attention is the real product; paragraph 2 lists features built to maximize engagement; paragraph 3 says attention-grabbing content does not necessarily serve users; paragraph 4 surveys responses and the burden on individuals. Targeted audiences are only a detail of paragraph 1, and reading habits are never measured.

exercises.prompt: In the writer's view, who is the real customer of a free platform?
choices: Its users
Governments
Advertisers
Subscribers
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the platforms' "real product is the attention of their users, which is sold to advertisers". If users' attention is the product being sold, the paying customers are the advertisers, not the users.

exercises.prompt: What does the writer imply by describing the systems as "engineered by teams of specialists to be irresistible"?
choices: Specialists should be banned from designing apps.
Individual willpower is a weak defense against such systems.
Disabling notifications is pointless.
Users enjoy the challenge of resisting well-designed apps.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: individual strategies "help", but they leave ordinary users to resist systems built by experts to be irresistible, so self-control alone is an unequal contest. Because they "help", they are not pointless.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "erode" is closest in meaning to …
choices: suddenly destroy
accurately measure
gradually wear away
openly reveal
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "Over time" an engagement-driven environment "may erode the capacity for sustained concentration" — a slow weakening, not a sudden destruction.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main argument of the passage?
choices: Free digital platforms are a generous public service.
Users can easily protect themselves by changing their settings.
Advertising is the only possible way to fund digital services.
A business model based on selling attention rewards design that may harm users and society.
exercises.explain: Paragraphs 1–3 trace a line from selling attention, to engagement-maximizing features, to content that does not serve users and may damage concentration. Paragraph 4 mentions subscriptions as an alternative and says individual strategies place an unfair burden on users.

exercises.statement: The writer suggests that the content that spreads most widely is not always the most useful to users.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: content that captures attention "is not necessarily content that serves users well", and outrage often spreads faster than careful reporting.

exercises.statement: According to the text, attention is now more abundant than information.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: information is abundant; attention is the scarce resource.

exercises.statement: Most users are unaware that their attention is sold to advertisers.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 explains the business model, but the passage never says what users know or do not know about it.

exercises.prompt: Endless feeds never reach a natural stopping ___.
choices: point
price
place
exercises.explain: Đoạn 2: "endless feeds that never reach a natural stopping point".

exercises.text: When information is plentiful, human attention becomes the ___ resource. Free platforms make money by selling that attention to ___, so they build features that keep users ___ for as long as possible. Emotionally charged material tends to win, which, critics fear, may weaken our ability to ___ for long periods.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: attention is the scarce resource and is sold to advertisers; paragraph 2: features "maximize engagement"; paragraph 3: critics argue this may erode "the capacity for sustained concentration".

lessons.title: Hiệu ứng giả dược
lessons.summary: Niềm tin có thể chữa bệnh đến đâu.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: A placebo is a treatment with no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill, given in place of real medicine. Yet patients who receive placebos frequently report genuine improvements, particularly in conditions involving pain, nausea or fatigue. This phenomenon, known as the placebo effect, has fascinated and frustrated researchers for decades.
paragraphs.vi: Giả dược là phương pháp điều trị không có hoạt chất, như viên thuốc đường, được đưa thay cho thuốc thật. Thế nhưng bệnh nhân dùng giả dược thường cho biết có cải thiện thật, nhất là với các tình trạng liên quan đến đau, buồn nôn hay mệt mỏi. Hiện tượng này, gọi là hiệu ứng giả dược, đã khiến giới nghiên cứu vừa say mê vừa bực bội suốt nhiều thập kỷ.

paragraphs.en: The effect is not simply imaginary. Brain imaging has shown that expecting relief can trigger the release of the body's own pain-reducing chemicals. Context matters too: an injection often produces a stronger placebo response than a pill, and an expensive-looking tablet can outperform an identical one that appears cheap.
paragraphs.vi: Hiệu ứng này không đơn thuần là tưởng tượng. Chụp ảnh não cho thấy kỳ vọng được giảm đau có thể kích hoạt cơ thể tiết ra chất giảm đau tự nhiên. Bối cảnh cũng quan trọng: tiêm thường tạo phản ứng giả dược mạnh hơn uống thuốc, và viên thuốc trông đắt tiền có thể hiệu quả hơn viên giống hệt nhưng trông rẻ.

paragraphs.en: Perhaps most surprisingly, some trials have found that placebos can help even when patients are told openly that they are taking an inactive pill. Researchers suspect that the ritual of treatment, including attention from a caring practitioner, contributes to the benefit.
paragraphs.vi: Có lẽ bất ngờ nhất, một số thử nghiệm phát hiện giả dược vẫn có thể giúp ích ngay cả khi bệnh nhân được nói thẳng rằng họ đang uống viên không có hoạt chất. Các nhà nghiên cứu ngờ rằng nghi thức điều trị, bao gồm sự quan tâm của người chữa bệnh tận tâm, góp phần vào lợi ích đó.

paragraphs.en: For medical science, however, the placebo effect is also an obstacle. To prove that a new drug works, researchers must show that it performs better than a placebo in carefully controlled trials. It is important, too, to recognize the limits: placebos may ease symptoms, but there is no evidence that they shrink tumors or cure infections.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên với y học, hiệu ứng giả dược cũng là trở ngại. Để chứng minh một loại thuốc mới có tác dụng, nhà nghiên cứu phải cho thấy nó hiệu quả hơn giả dược trong các thử nghiệm được kiểm soát chặt chẽ. Cũng cần nhận ra giới hạn: giả dược có thể làm dịu triệu chứng, nhưng không có bằng chứng nó làm teo khối u hay chữa nhiễm trùng.

headings: A hurdle for drug testing, and where the effect stops
Biological and contextual evidence that the effect is real
Why injections are more popular than pills
Real improvements from a treatment with nothing in it
How doctors decide when to prescribe placebos
Benefits that survive honesty about the treatment
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 defines the placebo and its genuine effects; paragraph 2 gives brain-imaging and context evidence; paragraph 3 describes placebos that work even when patients are told the truth; paragraph 4 presents the effect as an obstacle for trials and sets its limits. Injections are only a detail of paragraph 2, and prescribing decisions are not discussed.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred from the comparison between an expensive-looking tablet and an identical one that looks cheap?
choices: Expensive tablets contain more of the active ingredient.
Cheap tablets are produced less carefully.
Patients' beliefs about a treatment can change how well it seems to work.
Patients generally prefer pills to injections.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: the two tablets are "identical", so the only difference is how they look; a better result for the expensive-looking one must come from what patients expect, which fits the point that "expecting relief" triggers real effects.

exercises.prompt: What does the finding about patients who are told openly that their pill is inactive suggest?
choices: The benefit cannot depend only on patients being deceived.
Those patients secretly believed the pills were real medicine.
Caring practitioners make real drugs unnecessary.
Telling patients the truth makes treatment less effective.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: placebos helped "even when patients are told openly" that the pill is inactive, so deception is not the whole explanation; researchers point instead to the ritual of treatment and a caring practitioner.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word "ease" is closest in meaning to …
choices: explain
relieve
disguise
worsen
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "placebos may ease symptoms, but … no evidence that they shrink tumors or cure infections" — they can make symptoms less severe without curing the disease.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer point out that placebos do not shrink tumors or cure infections?
choices: To show that placebos are useless
To explain why drug trials use placebos
To argue that placebos should replace real medicine for minor conditions
To warn against overstating what placebos can do
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "It is important, too, to recognize the limits" — after three paragraphs on the surprising power of placebos, the writer marks where that power ends. Placebos are not useless, since they "may ease symptoms".

exercises.statement: Deceiving patients is not always necessary for a placebo to have an effect.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: some trials found placebos helped even when patients knew the pill was inactive.

exercises.statement: The writer presents the placebo effect as helpful to medical science in every respect.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "For medical science, however, the placebo effect is also an obstacle", because new drugs must outperform it in trials.

exercises.statement: Women respond more strongly to placebos than men.
exercises.explain: The passage never compares men and women.

exercises.prompt: An expensive-looking tablet can outperform an identical one that appears ___.
choices: cheap
large
bitter
exercises.explain: Đoạn 2: "an identical one that appears cheap".

exercises.text: A placebo contains no active ___, yet patients often feel genuinely better after taking one. Brain scans show that the mere ___ of relief can release the body's own painkillers. Because a new drug must ___ a placebo in controlled trials, the effect also makes research harder; and while placebos can soothe symptoms, nothing suggests they can cure ___.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: a placebo has "no active ingredient"; paragraph 2: "expecting relief" triggers pain-reducing chemicals; paragraph 4: a drug must perform "better than a placebo", and there is no evidence placebos "cure infections".

lessons.title: Thành phố 15 phút
lessons.summary: Quy hoạch để mọi thứ trong tầm đi bộ.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: For much of the twentieth century, urban planning in many countries was organized around the private car. Residential suburbs, office districts and shopping centers were deliberately separated, linked by wide roads that made driving convenient and walking impractical.
paragraphs.vi: Trong phần lớn thế kỷ hai mươi, quy hoạch đô thị ở nhiều nước được tổ chức xoay quanh ô tô cá nhân. Khu dân cư ngoại ô, khu văn phòng và trung tâm mua sắm bị cố ý tách biệt, nối với nhau bằng những con đường rộng khiến lái xe tiện lợi và đi bộ bất tiện.

paragraphs.en: The "fifteen-minute city" proposes a different logic. Its central idea is that residents should be able to reach most daily necessities, such as groceries, schools, clinics, parks and workplaces, within a short walk or bicycle ride from home. Rather than building a single dominant center, planners aim for a network of complete, mixed-use neighborhoods.
paragraphs.vi: "Thành phố 15 phút" đề xuất một logic khác. Ý tưởng trung tâm là cư dân có thể đến được hầu hết nhu cầu thiết yếu hằng ngày, như cửa hàng thực phẩm, trường học, phòng khám, công viên và nơi làm việc, chỉ bằng một quãng đi bộ hay đạp xe ngắn từ nhà. Thay vì xây một trung tâm duy nhất áp đảo, nhà quy hoạch hướng tới một mạng lưới các khu phố đầy đủ, đa chức năng.

paragraphs.en: Supporters point to a range of benefits: less traffic and pollution, more physical activity, and stronger local communities as people spend more time in their own neighborhoods. The concept also has an equity dimension, since households without cars are often the most disadvantaged by car-centered design.
paragraphs.vi: Người ủng hộ chỉ ra nhiều lợi ích: ít giao thông và ô nhiễm hơn, vận động nhiều hơn, cộng đồng địa phương gắn kết hơn khi người dân dành nhiều thời gian hơn ở khu phố mình. Khái niệm này còn có khía cạnh công bằng, vì những hộ không có xe thường chịu thiệt nhiều nhất từ thiết kế lấy ô tô làm trung tâm.

paragraphs.en: Implementation, though, raises difficult questions. Improving a neighborhood can push up property prices and displace the very residents it was meant to serve. Moreover, specialized jobs and services cannot exist in every district, so good public transport between neighborhoods remains essential. The model, in other words, complements city-wide planning rather than replacing it.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên, triển khai đặt ra những câu hỏi khó. Cải thiện một khu phố có thể đẩy giá bất động sản lên và khiến chính những cư dân mà nó định phục vụ phải dời đi. Hơn nữa, việc làm và dịch vụ chuyên biệt không thể có ở mọi quận, nên giao thông công cộng tốt giữa các khu vẫn là thiết yếu. Nói cách khác, mô hình này bổ sung chứ không thay thế quy hoạch toàn thành phố.

headings: Everyday needs within easy reach
Why suburbs became more popular than city centers
Practical obstacles and the model's proper place
A past built around driving
Gains for health, community and fairness
The rising cost of public transport
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 describes car-centered planning; paragraph 2 sets out the core idea of nearby daily needs; paragraph 3 lists the benefits, including equity; paragraph 4 covers problems of implementation and concludes that the model complements city-wide planning. The popularity of suburbs and the cost of transport are never discussed.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred from the warning that improving a neighborhood may "displace the very residents it was meant to serve"?
choices: Property prices usually fall when parks and clinics are added.
Planners deliberately aim to replace poorer residents.
The benefits of an improvement could go mainly to newer, wealthier residents.
Residents generally oppose improvements to their neighborhoods.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: improvements "push up property prices", so original residents who cannot afford them may have to leave, and the people who enjoy the improved area may be newcomers who can. The improvement was "meant to serve" the original residents, so it is not a deliberate aim.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "equity" is closest in meaning to …
choices: ownership
efficiency
value
fairness
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: the "equity dimension" is explained by the fact that households without cars are the most disadvantaged by car-centered design — a question of fairness, not of ownership or financial value.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer mention specialized jobs and services in paragraph 4?
choices: To explain why good links between neighborhoods are still needed
To argue that the model only suits highly skilled workers
To show that every district can become self-sufficient
To criticize planners for ignoring employment
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: specialized jobs and services "cannot exist in every district, so good public transport between neighborhoods remains essential". The point is a limit of the model, which leads to the conclusion that it complements city-wide planning.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best reflects the writer's conclusion about the fifteen-minute city?
choices: It should replace city-wide planning altogether.
It can be a useful part of city planning but cannot work on its own.
It has failed wherever it has been tried.
It matters only for households without cars.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "The model, in other words, complements city-wide planning rather than replacing it." The passage reports no failed trials, and paragraph 3 lists benefits for everyone, not only households without cars.

exercises.statement: Twentieth-century planning made it harder to get around on foot.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: wide roads made driving convenient and "walking impractical".

exercises.statement: According to the writer, a well-designed neighborhood can make travel to other districts unnecessary.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: specialized jobs and services cannot exist in every district, so public transport between neighborhoods "remains essential".

exercises.statement: The fifteen-minute city was first tested in a European capital.
exercises.explain: The passage never says where the model was first tried.

exercises.prompt: Improving a neighborhood can push up property prices and ___ existing residents.
choices: displace
attract
employ
exercises.explain: Đoạn 4: "displace the very residents it was meant to serve".

exercises.text: Twentieth-century planning kept homes, offices and shops ___, which suited drivers rather than pedestrians. The fifteen-minute city instead imagines a network of ___ neighborhoods where daily needs are close at hand. Supporters expect cleaner air and closer communities, but rising property prices could push out ___, and transport between districts remains ___.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: functions were "deliberately separated"; paragraph 2: "complete, mixed-use neighborhoods"; paragraph 4: improvements can "displace the very residents it was meant to serve", and public transport "remains essential".

lessons.title: Thuật toán có công bằng?
lessons.summary: Đạo đức của máy ra quyết định.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Automated systems now help decide who is offered a loan, which job applicants are interviewed and how resources are allocated in public services. Their appeal is easy to understand: unlike human officials, algorithms do not get tired, and they apply the same rules to everyone.
paragraphs.vi: Hệ thống tự động nay giúp quyết định ai được vay vốn, ứng viên nào được phỏng vấn và nguồn lực được phân bổ thế nào trong dịch vụ công. Sức hút của chúng dễ hiểu: khác với cán bộ là con người, thuật toán không mệt mỏi và áp dụng cùng một quy tắc cho mọi người.

paragraphs.en: Consistency, however, is not the same as fairness. Many systems learn by detecting patterns in historical data, and if past decisions were shaped by prejudice, the system may faithfully reproduce it. A hiring tool trained on the profiles of previous successful employees, for example, may learn to favor candidates who resemble them, regardless of ability.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên, nhất quán không đồng nghĩa với công bằng. Nhiều hệ thống học bằng cách phát hiện quy luật trong dữ liệu quá khứ, và nếu quyết định trước đây bị định kiến chi phối thì hệ thống có thể tái tạo nguyên vẹn định kiến đó. Ví dụ, một công cụ tuyển dụng được huấn luyện bằng hồ sơ của các nhân viên thành công trước đây có thể học cách ưu ái ứng viên giống họ, bất kể năng lực.

paragraphs.en: Removing sensitive information is rarely a complete solution. Even if a system is not told an applicant's gender or ethnicity, other variables, such as postal code or the clubs someone belongs to, can act as indirect substitutes. Furthermore, researchers have demonstrated that several reasonable mathematical definitions of fairness cannot all be satisfied at once, which means that designers must make value judgments, not merely technical ones.
paragraphs.vi: Xoá thông tin nhạy cảm hiếm khi là giải pháp trọn vẹn. Ngay cả khi hệ thống không được biết giới tính hay sắc tộc của ứng viên, các biến khác như mã bưu chính hay câu lạc bộ người đó tham gia có thể đóng vai trò thay thế gián tiếp. Hơn nữa, các nhà nghiên cứu đã chứng minh một số định nghĩa toán học hợp lý về công bằng không thể cùng lúc được thoả mãn, nghĩa là người thiết kế phải đưa ra phán đoán giá trị chứ không chỉ phán đoán kỹ thuật.

paragraphs.en: For this reason, many experts call for transparency about how such systems work, regular independent audits, and a meaningful right for individuals to challenge automated decisions that affect them.
paragraphs.vi: Vì lý do đó, nhiều chuyên gia kêu gọi minh bạch về cách các hệ thống này vận hành, kiểm định độc lập định kỳ, và quyền thực chất cho cá nhân được khiếu nại các quyết định tự động ảnh hưởng đến họ.

headings: Why there is no simple technical fix
Proof that human officials are fairer than machines
Why automated decisions seem attractive
How banks calculate loan risk
Safeguards that experts are calling for
How past prejudice can be built into a system
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 explains the appeal of algorithms; paragraph 2 shows how biased historical data can be reproduced; paragraph 3 explains why deleting sensitive data and choosing a definition of fairness are not purely technical; paragraph 4 lists the safeguards experts want. Loans are only an example in paragraph 1, and humans are never shown to be fairer.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer give the example of a hiring tool trained on previous employees?
choices: To prove that hiring tools are less accurate than human recruiters
To argue that companies should stop keeping employee profiles
To show that algorithms get tired of repetitive tasks
To show how a system can repeat past unfairness while applying its rules consistently
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 opens with "Consistency, however, is not the same as fairness", and the hiring tool illustrates this: it treats everyone by the same learned pattern, yet favors people who resemble past employees "regardless of ability". Paragraph 1 says algorithms do not get tired.

exercises.prompt: A company removes gender from its hiring data, but its system still favors men. Based on the passage, which explanation is most likely?
choices: Other variables in the data are closely linked to gender.
The system was told the applicants' gender by mistake.
The system became tired after processing many applications.
Consistent rules always produce unfair results.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: even when a system "is not told an applicant's gender", variables such as postal code or club membership "can act as indirect substitutes". Paragraph 1 rules out tiredness, and the passage says consistency does not guarantee fairness, not that it always produces unfairness.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "faithfully" is closest in meaning to …
choices: loyally
hopefully
exactly
reluctantly
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: the system "may faithfully reproduce" past prejudice — it copies it exactly. "Loyally" is another meaning of the word, but it does not fit a system copying patterns.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the writer's argument?
choices: Algorithms should replace human officials because they never get tired.
Treating everyone by the same rules does not by itself make automated decisions fair, so oversight is needed.
Automated systems are unfair mainly because they are badly programmed.
Fairness can be achieved simply by deleting sensitive data.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: consistency is not fairness; paragraph 3: deleting sensitive data is "rarely a complete solution" and value judgments are unavoidable; paragraph 4: experts therefore call for transparency, audits and a right to challenge. The problem lies in data and values, not bad programming.

exercises.statement: Information that seems neutral can still reveal sensitive characteristics indirectly.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: variables such as postal code or club membership "can act as indirect substitutes" for gender or ethnicity.

exercises.statement: The writer argues that consistency guarantees fairness.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "Consistency, however, is not the same as fairness."

exercises.statement: Automated hiring tools are cheaper to run than human recruiters.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 says algorithms do not get tired and apply the same rules, but the passage never compares costs.

exercises.prompt: Experts call for regular independent ___ of automated systems.
choices: audits
upgrades
advertisements
exercises.explain: Đoạn 4: "regular independent audits".

exercises.text: Automated systems appeal because they never tire and treat everyone by the same ___. Yet if they learn from records shaped by ___, they may copy past unfairness. Deleting sensitive details seldom solves this, since other information can serve as a ___. And because competing definitions of fairness cannot all be met at once, designers must make choices about ___ as well as technique.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: algorithms "apply the same rules to everyone"; paragraph 2: past decisions "shaped by prejudice" can be reproduced; paragraph 3: other variables act as "indirect substitutes", and designers must make "value judgments, not merely technical ones".

lessons.title: Ngôn ngữ và tư duy
lessons.summary: Ngôn ngữ có định hình cách ta nghĩ?

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: The idea that the language we speak influences the way we think, often called linguistic relativity, has had a turbulent history. In its strongest form, it claimed that language determines thought, so that speakers of different languages inhabit fundamentally different mental worlds. This version has been largely abandoned, not least because people clearly can think about things for which their language has no word.
paragraphs.vi: Ý tưởng rằng ngôn ngữ ta nói ảnh hưởng đến cách ta nghĩ, thường gọi là thuyết tương đối ngôn ngữ, có một lịch sử đầy sóng gió. Ở dạng mạnh nhất, nó cho rằng ngôn ngữ quyết định tư duy, khiến người nói các ngôn ngữ khác nhau sống trong những thế giới tinh thần khác biệt căn bản. Phiên bản này phần lớn đã bị từ bỏ, không chỉ vì con người rõ ràng có thể nghĩ về những thứ mà ngôn ngữ của họ không có từ để gọi.

paragraphs.en: A weaker version, however, has found considerable experimental support. Some languages describe location using fixed directions, such as north and south, rather than terms like left and right. Speakers of such languages tend to keep track of compass directions with remarkable accuracy, even indoors, presumably because their everyday speech requires it.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên, một phiên bản yếu hơn đã nhận được sự ủng hộ đáng kể từ thực nghiệm. Một số ngôn ngữ mô tả vị trí bằng phương hướng cố định như bắc và nam thay vì trái và phải. Người nói những ngôn ngữ này có xu hướng định hướng la bàn chính xác đáng kinh ngạc, ngay cả trong nhà, có lẽ vì lời nói hằng ngày của họ đòi hỏi điều đó.

paragraphs.en: Similar findings have emerged for color. Languages divide the spectrum differently, and when a language has separate basic words for two shades, its speakers are often slightly faster at distinguishing them. The differences are measurable but modest: no one is unable to perceive a color simply because they lack a word for it.
paragraphs.vi: Phát hiện tương tự cũng xuất hiện với màu sắc. Các ngôn ngữ chia quang phổ khác nhau, và khi một ngôn ngữ có từ cơ bản riêng cho hai sắc độ, người nói thường phân biệt chúng nhanh hơn một chút. Khác biệt đo được nhưng khiêm tốn: không ai mất khả năng nhìn thấy một màu chỉ vì thiếu từ gọi tên nó.

paragraphs.en: The current consensus, then, is nuanced. Language does not imprison thought, but it acts as a set of habits, directing attention toward some distinctions and away from others.
paragraphs.vi: Vậy đồng thuận hiện nay khá tinh tế. Ngôn ngữ không giam cầm tư duy, nhưng hoạt động như một tập hợp thói quen, hướng sự chú ý tới một số phân biệt và rời khỏi những phân biệt khác.

headings: Language as a guide to attention, not a prison
Why some languages have more color words than others
How describing space can sharpen a sense of direction
An extreme claim that has fallen out of favor
Teaching children to use a compass
Small but real effects on color perception
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 explains why the strong version has been abandoned; paragraph 2 gives the evidence on fixed directions; paragraph 3 reports modest color effects; paragraph 4 states the nuanced consensus. The passage does not explain why languages differ in color words and never mentions children.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the current consensus?
choices: Language has no effect on thought.
Language completely determines thought.
Language directs attention through habits but does not imprison thought.
Only bilingual people are influenced by language.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "Language does not imprison thought, but it acts as a set of habits, directing attention toward some distinctions and away from others."

exercises.prompt: What does the word "presumably" in paragraph 2 show about the explanation that follows it?
choices: It has been disproved by later studies.
It is a likely interpretation rather than a proven fact.
It applies only to people indoors.
It is the explanation preferred by the speakers themselves.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: speakers track compass directions accurately, "presumably because their everyday speech requires it". The writer offers this cause as reasonable but unproven; nothing says it was disproved or that the speakers gave it.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 1, the word "turbulent" is closest in meaning to …
choices: brief
respected
forgotten
troubled
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the idea has had a "turbulent history" — its strongest form was claimed and then "largely abandoned", a history full of conflict and change.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer include the example of languages that use fixed compass directions?
choices: To provide evidence for a weaker version of linguistic relativity
To show that the strong version is correct after all
To explain how languages develop words for direction
To argue that "left" and "right" are unnecessary words
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 begins "A weaker version, however, has found considerable experimental support", and the compass example is that support. Paragraph 1 has already said the strong version was abandoned.

exercises.statement: The writer suggests that everyday speech habits can train a particular mental skill.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: speakers of fixed-direction languages track compass directions accurately, "presumably because their everyday speech requires it".

exercises.statement: People cannot perceive a color if their language has no word for it.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "no one is unable to perceive a color simply because they lack a word for it."

exercises.statement: Languages with more color words are easier for children to learn.
exercises.explain: The passage never discusses how children learn languages.

exercises.prompt: The color differences are measurable but ___.
choices: modest
enormous
permanent
exercises.explain: Đoạn 3: "The differences are measurable but modest".

exercises.text: The bold claim that language ___ thought has been largely abandoned. A weaker version fares better: people whose language relies on fixed directions keep track of ___ with striking accuracy, and having separate words for two shades makes people slightly quicker to ___ them. These effects are real but small; rather than a prison, language is better seen as a set of ___ that guide attention.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the strong form said language "determines thought"; paragraph 2: speakers track compass directions accurately; paragraph 3: speakers are faster at "distinguishing" shades; paragraph 4: language acts as "a set of habits, directing attention".

lessons.title: Ý niệm về tiến bộ
lessons.summary: Lịch sử của niềm tin rằng tương lai sẽ tốt hơn.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: To many people today, it seems natural to assume that the future will be better than the past: that knowledge will grow, technology will improve and living standards will rise. Historically, however, this expectation is relatively unusual. Many earlier societies understood time as cyclical, with ages of prosperity and decline repeating endlessly, or believed that humanity had fallen from an earlier golden age.
paragraphs.vi: Với nhiều người ngày nay, việc cho rằng tương lai sẽ tốt hơn quá khứ có vẻ hiển nhiên: tri thức sẽ tăng, công nghệ sẽ cải tiến và mức sống sẽ nâng cao. Tuy nhiên, xét về lịch sử, kỳ vọng này tương đối khác thường. Nhiều xã hội trước đây hiểu thời gian theo vòng tuần hoàn, các thời kỳ thịnh vượng và suy tàn lặp lại mãi, hoặc tin rằng nhân loại đã sa sút từ một thời hoàng kim xưa.

paragraphs.en: The modern idea of progress took shape gradually, gaining momentum as the natural sciences produced cumulative results. If each generation of researchers could build on the discoveries of the last, it seemed reasonable to hope that moral and political life might advance in a similar way, through reason and education.
paragraphs.vi: Ý niệm hiện đại về tiến bộ hình thành dần dần, có đà khi khoa học tự nhiên tạo ra kết quả tích luỹ. Nếu mỗi thế hệ nhà nghiên cứu có thể xây dựng trên phát hiện của thế hệ trước, thì có vẻ hợp lý khi hy vọng đời sống đạo đức và chính trị cũng có thể tiến lên tương tự, nhờ lý trí và giáo dục.

paragraphs.en: The twentieth century severely tested this optimism. Technological sophistication proved entirely compatible with devastating wars, and industrial growth brought environmental damage that earlier thinkers had barely imagined. Some philosophers concluded that the belief in progress had been naive, or even dangerous, since it could be used to justify sacrificing present lives for a promised future.
paragraphs.vi: Thế kỷ hai mươi đã thử thách nặng nề sự lạc quan này. Trình độ công nghệ tinh vi tỏ ra hoàn toàn có thể song hành với những cuộc chiến tàn khốc, và tăng trưởng công nghiệp đem lại tổn hại môi trường mà các nhà tư tưởng trước đó khó hình dung. Một số triết gia kết luận niềm tin vào tiến bộ là ngây thơ, thậm chí nguy hiểm, vì nó có thể bị dùng để biện minh cho việc hy sinh những sinh mạng hiện tại vì một tương lai được hứa hẹn.

paragraphs.en: Today, many thinkers adopt a more cautious position. Measurable improvements in areas such as life expectancy and literacy are real, they argue, but they are neither inevitable nor irreversible. Progress, on this view, is not a law of history but an achievement that each generation must work to sustain.
paragraphs.vi: Ngày nay nhiều nhà tư tưởng chọn lập trường thận trọng hơn. Họ cho rằng những cải thiện đo lường được trong các lĩnh vực như tuổi thọ và tỷ lệ biết chữ là có thật, nhưng chúng không tất yếu cũng không phải không thể đảo ngược. Theo quan điểm này, tiến bộ không phải quy luật của lịch sử mà là thành tựu mà mỗi thế hệ phải nỗ lực duy trì.

headings: Science as the model for wider advance
How ancient societies measured time
Progress as something to be maintained, not guaranteed
A modern assumption with few historical parallels
The environmental costs of modern industry
A century that shook confidence
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 shows that expecting a better future is historically unusual; paragraph 2 links the idea to cumulative science; paragraph 3 describes how the twentieth century tested this optimism; paragraph 4 presents progress as an achievement to sustain. Environmental damage is only one detail of paragraph 3, and ancient methods of measuring time are not discussed.

exercises.prompt: What role does the reference to the natural sciences play in paragraph 2?
choices: It shows that science and morality are unrelated.
It proves that political life advanced as quickly as science.
It explains why people began to expect improvement in other areas of life.
It criticizes scientists for neglecting education.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: because researchers could build on earlier discoveries, "it seemed reasonable to hope" that moral and political life might advance in the same way. Science is the model, and the paragraph speaks only of hope, not proof.

exercises.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraphs 2 and 3 about the optimism that the twentieth century "severely tested"?
choices: It had predicted the environmental damage caused by industry.
It rested on the expectation that moral life would advance alongside knowledge.
It was based on a cyclical view of history.
It was abandoned by every philosopher after the wars.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: people hoped moral and political life would advance like science; paragraph 3: technological sophistication "proved entirely compatible with devastating wars", which tested that hope. Earlier thinkers had "barely imagined" the environmental damage, and only "some philosophers" rejected progress.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "momentum" is closest in meaning to …
choices: critics
strength
funding
precision
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: the idea of progress took shape gradually, "gaining momentum" as science produced cumulative results — it grew stronger and spread faster.

exercises.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
choices: Why modern societies are better than earlier ones
How science replaced philosophy
Why wars became more destructive in the twentieth century
How the belief in progress arose, was challenged and has been reconsidered
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 places the belief in history, paragraph 2 shows how it arose, paragraph 3 how it was challenged, and paragraph 4 the more cautious view held today. Wars are only one piece of evidence in paragraph 3.

exercises.statement: Some thinkers feared that faith in a better future could be used to excuse harm in the present.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: the belief "could be used to justify sacrificing present lives for a promised future".

exercises.statement: The cautious view holds that improvements in life expectancy are inevitable.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: such improvements are real but "neither inevitable nor irreversible".

exercises.statement: Literacy rates have doubled over the last fifty years.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4 says literacy has measurably improved but gives no figures or time period.

exercises.prompt: On the cautious view, progress is an achievement that each generation must work to ___.
choices: sustain
predict
reject
exercises.explain: Câu cuối: "an achievement that each generation must work to sustain".

exercises.text: Expecting the future to improve on the past feels obvious today, but it is historically ___: many earlier cultures saw time as repeating, or as a fall from a golden age. The idea grew as scientific discoveries ___ from one generation to the next. After the wars and environmental harm of the twentieth century, some philosophers judged it ___ or even dangerous. Many thinkers now see progress as real but ___, something each generation must protect.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the expectation is "relatively unusual"; paragraph 2: science produced "cumulative results"; paragraph 3: some philosophers called the belief "naive, or even dangerous"; paragraph 4: improvements are "neither inevitable nor irreversible".
